local_facts.claim: Overland Park has a median year built of 1989. The city therefore contains a broad mix of older, limited-clearance garages and later sectional-door installations rather than one uniform housing era.
local_facts.why_it_matters: The garage age helps predict the spring type, headroom and track arrangement. That lets a technician prepare torsion, extension or low-headroom hardware before arriving instead of treating every Overland Park garage as identical.
local_facts.title: A 1989 median build year means more than one garage setup

local_facts.claim: Overland Park says it reviews residential construction plans and documents that require a building permit, and requires contractors to have an active Johnson County contractor license to receive a building permit for work in the city.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A routine spring, cable, roller or opener repair works on existing hardware. A project that changes structural framing or enlarges a garage opening may enter the city permit process, so the scope should be confirmed before a replacement door is ordered.
local_facts.title: An altered garage opening can become a permit project

local_facts.claim: On January 24, 2026, NWS Kansas City/Pleasant Hill listed Overland Park in a Johnson County winter storm warning and cold weather advisory, with wind chills forecast as low as 17 below zero and four to six inches of additional snow forecast in the warning.
local_facts.why_it_matters: A hard cold snap does not create spring fatigue from nothing, but it can expose a spring already near its cycle limit. Cold-thickened lubricant, a frozen bottom seal and the first lift of the morning add resistance that makes an aged torsion system more likely to fail.
local_facts.title: The January 2026 cold snap was a real mechanical stress test
